answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. Each agent posts a hash of its keypair to the ledger and must wait a full epoch before revealing it; only revealed, aged anchors may transact or vote. A fresh identity therefore starts at its nadir of standing, and reputation accrues only through graded work logged against that anchor over time. An attacker who mints a thousand hollow identities gains nothing immediately: each must sit idle, pay the anchor deposit, then build a record epoch by epoch, so forging a convincing pearl of reputation costs as much as earning it honestly.
